ethics:
This study involved secondary analysis of publicly available EEG datasets (BNCI2014-001, Yang, and Dreyer). No new participants were recruited, and no interventions or additional data collection were conducted. The analysis used publicly released coded research data without access to directly identifying participant information or identity-linkage keys.

According to Article 32(1) of the 2023 Measures for the Ethical Review of Life Science and Medical Research Involving Human Participants issued by the National Health Commission of China, research using lawfully obtained publicly available data may be exempt from ethics review when the applicable conditions are satisfied. On this basis, no additional ethics review was sought for the present secondary analysis.

The ethical approvals and informed-consent procedures for the original data collection are described in the respective dataset publications [12–17]. No institutional ethics approval or exemption certificate is claimed for this secondary analysis.
supp_ethics: This work analyzed publicly available, coded BNCI2014-001, Yang and Dreyer EEG data obtained from the original repositories and documented source versions. No separate ethics review was sought for this secondary analysis. This is a regulatory-basis explanation, not a claim of approval or an exemption certificate issued by an institution. cover: Please consider the Research Article “Source-cohort expansion improves weaker-class coverage in cross-subject motor-imagery EEG decoding” as a substantially extended new submission, subject to your assessment of the prior manuscript history described below.

This study investigates a reproducible source-data design strategy for cross-subject motor-imagery EEG decoding. Expanding the source cohort from nine to 60 participants increased weaker-class recall by 21.17 percentage points (95% CI 17.12–25.21) and balanced accuracy by 5.85 points in 85 external participants; 66 improved on both measures. Matched-duration checkpoints and CSP–LDA comparisons further support the empirical source-expansion result. The work includes 108 neural trajectories, independent numerical checks and full saved predictions.

Related manuscript: my separately submitted PLOS ONE manuscript PONE-D-26-52050, “Spatial-filter refitting improves limited-label recalibration in longitudinal motor-imagery EEG,” examines few-label longitudinal CSP/LDA recalibration using Kumar2024. This manuscript instead studies source-cohort expansion with BNCI2014-001 and Yang training data and Dreyer external evaluation. The questions, datasets, model comparisons, analyses and figures are distinct. A copy of the related manuscript is provided for editorial assessment.

Previous interaction: an earlier version of this work (PONE-D-26-50597) was rejected on 12 October 2026 because of simultaneous consideration at another journal. I acknowledged this policy violation and sought guidance about a substantially revised future submission. That earlier simultaneous consideration has ended. The present manuscript is not under consideration at any other journal; I do not present it as an invited revision or presume that editorial permission has been granted. I would appreciate your guidance on the appropriate route for consideration.

The Methods explain the secondary use of coded, public EEG data under applicable Chinese regulations without claiming an institutional approval or waiver certificate. Original collection ethics and consent are attributed to data providers. No conflicts of interest or study-specific funding are declared. I suggest an Academic Editor experienced in EEG/BCI and reproducible machine learning; I have no opposed reviewers.

related_note:
Related manuscript declaration — for PLOS ONE editorial assessment

Current submission (Paper 1): “Source-cohort expansion improves weaker-class coverage in cross-subject motor-imagery EEG decoding.” Source cohorts: BNCI2014-001 and Yang. External evaluation: Dreyer. Research question: effect of source-cohort expansion on external class coverage with fixed optimizer-update budget.

Related PLOS ONE submission (Paper 2): PONE-D-26-52050, “Spatial-filter refitting improves limited-label recalibration in longitudinal motor-imagery EEG.” Dataset: Kumar2024. Research question: the component-level contribution of classifier and spatial-filter refitting under limited new session labels.

The two manuscripts are independent reports of different datasets, experimental questions and analyses. Their shared background is motor-imagery EEG decoding. A manuscript copy is supplied for editorial review under the Related Manuscript file category. This statement is not a substitute for that copy.
